newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Stable with Chinese support seen.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Stable with Chinese support seen.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was stable on Tuesday but sentiment was supported following some import interest from China, traders said.
Fresh demand has been steady from a local trader as well as a major, supporting sentiment over the past few weeks, while firmer overnight crude values also helped, they said.
However, at least some five cargoes are scheduled to arrive in Singapore from the Middle East and the Mediterranean in June, adding pressure on prices, they said.
"Those cargoes are still looking for buyers and that could depress prices a little," said one trader.
Enquiries from Chinese buyers have been heard recently at around $6-$7 per tonne above Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight South China basis, traders said.
"Chinese enquiries should continue to be quite good in the near term," said one trader.
"But their offers are very low," said another trader. "The freight is about $7.5-$8 per tonne, so the $6-$7 premium is not enough."

On the supply side, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of three-percent, 180-cst grade sulphur fuel oil for first half July lifting, free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung.
The tender closes on June 10 and will be valid for two days. From Indonesia, the market is expecting demand to increase in July, traders said.

Indonesia is expected to raise its imports in July and August due to the scheduled shutdown of a 200,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit at the 265,000-bpd Balikpapan refinery for one month from July 10.
It has also scheduled to shut down a 100,000-bpd crude unit at its Cilacap refinery for 35 days beginning August 13.
In the fuel oil swaps market, June swaps were quoted at $101.00/$101.50 against Monday's $100.50/$101.25 and July swaps were at $100.00/$100.50 against $99.75/$100.25.
